issues.title: Incorrect table names
issues.problem: The query uses 'users' and 'orders' instead of the correct table names 'sigma_analytics.dim_customer' and 'sigma_analytics.fact_transactions'.
issues.fix:
SELECT c.customer_name, c.email, t.transaction_id
FROM sigma_analytics.dim_customer c, sigma_analytics.fact_transactions t
WHERE c.customer_id = t.customer_id
AND t.amount > (
    SELECT AVG(amount)
    FROM sigma_analytics.fact_transactions
    WHERE customer_id = c.customer_id
);

issues.title: Correlated subquery
issues.problem: The correlated subquery can be inefficient as it runs for each row in the outer query.
issues.fix:
SELECT c.customer_name, c.email, t.transaction_id
FROM sigma_analytics.dim_customer c
JOIN (
    SELECT customer_id, AVG(amount) as avg_amount
    FROM sigma_analytics.fact_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id
) avg_orders ON c.customer_id = avg_orders.customer_id
JOIN sigma_analytics.fact_transactions t ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id
WHERE t.amount > avg_orders.avg_amount;

issues.title: Lack of table aliases
issues.problem: Using table aliases would make the query more readable.
issues.fix:
SELECT c.customer_name, c.email, t.transaction_id
FROM sigma_analytics.dim_customer c
JOIN (
    SELECT customer_id, AVG(amount) as avg_amount
    FROM sigma_analytics.fact_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id
) avg_orders ON c.customer_id = avg_orders.customer_id
JOIN sigma_analytics.fact_transactions t ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id
WHERE t.amount > avg_orders.avg_amount;

    FROM sigma_analytics.fact_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id

review.summary: The query had issues with incorrect table names, a correlated subquery affecting performance, and lack of readability due to missing table aliases.
